Throughout the 90s I upgraded my main PC many times since I has access to a lot of different hardware options that were reasonably priced through my work connections. Starting from a 12 MHz 80286 machine in '91 through my final 90s upgrade of a 400 MHz Pentium II, I think my best iteration was about midway through. When the Pentium processor line was first released, I was able to pick up a "defective" 60 MHz Pentium processor on the cheap. It was defective because of the famous Pentium FDiv bug and was pulled for replacement. I didn't mind the possibility that a rare floating point division operation could result in an inaccurate result so I bought the CPU and a motherboard to go with it. I upgraded my giant full tower case with the new board and saw a wonderful improvement in power and speed running Windows for Workgroups 3.11 (aand not longer after, Windows 95). Everything just ran great. That machine served me well until my Pentium 120 MHz upgrade a year or two later. I was a major hardware junkie back then. Here's what I recall that rig having:

  • Intel Pentium 60
  • Gigabyte MB (don't remember the model)
  • 8 MB RAM (yes, megabyte)
  • Diamond Multimedia Stealth32 video card
  • Gravis Ultrasound sound card (original and best GF-1 model)
  • Adaptec 2920 SCSI 1 adapter (all drives and other peripherals)
  • Quantum Fireball 540 MB (yes, megabyte) SCSI 1 HDD
  • Quantum Fireball 85 MB SCSI 1 HDD
  • NEC Multispin 4x SCSI CD-ROM drive (caddy-based, remember those?)
  • Colorado Memory Systems 250 tape drive (internal)
  • Iomega Bernoulli 20 MB SCSI removable cartridge drive (external, got for free)
  • UMax SCSI flatbed color scanner
  • Acecad AceCAT 12x12 digitizing tablet
  • 3Com 3C509 Ethernet NIC
  • HP Deskjet 1200c (open box item, paid $75)
  • NEC Multisync 3d 15" monitor (CRT of course)

I think I also owned an Iomega ZIP drive at that time too, but I'm not sure if it was this iteration or later. It was a fun time to build PCs back then. We don't seem to have the choice we did then and we certainly don't have the number of player in the game. Ah, good times.

*Edit: 400 MHz not 500 Mhz Pentium II
